H_P2_scaled.the_object: In the theorem-generated Boolean world, the affine/XOR row is (approximation=inapprox, parameterized=FPT) — hard-to-approximate yet FPT. The deceptive-terrain control is not an outlier here; on the v1 census it is the entire approx|parameterized axis. This connects to I6: affine is the SOLE bounded-width obstruction (Barto-Kozik), i.e. the one language that is easy to solve yet resists local consistency AND (Maltsev) is FPT while (Håstad) inapproximable.
H_P2_scaled.prediction: As the Boolean tier refines (0-/1-valid, S0^k/S1^k chains, intersections — the documented v1.1 roster expansion) so the both-real approx|parameterized table has many distinct rows, the association resolves to ONE of three pre-stated outcomes.
H_P2_scaled.decision_rule: On the SCALED census (>= a pre-set distinct-row floor to be fixed in the roster-expansion prereg), compute the both-real approx|parameterized Cramer's V with the CORRECTED permutation test (permute among the both-real rows only; selftest-locked) and R25-net the entailment-forced component. Then classify: (a) POSITIVE / canon-like — harder-approx co-occurs with harder-param (the canon's direction reproduces under generation); (b) REVERSED / affine-dominated — the decoupling generalizes beyond affine (hard-approx co-occurs with easy-param broadly); (c) STRATIFIED — the sign splits by co-clone stratum (e.g. positive within the NP-hard region, reversed on the tractable-but-inapproximable languages). This is the REAL P2.
H_P2_scaled.not_a_ruling_at_v1: The v1 direction-reversal is DESCRIPTIVE only and is NOT evidence that the canon's gradient is 'roster sociology' — Crucible S5 already retired that explanation on the actual canon (roster exhausted with every known violator; gradient survived at p=0.0001). A 7-row theorem-world anecdote cannot reinstate a hypothesis a dedicated adversarial attack on the real data has retired.
